transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morris (Redwood SE), Rachel Nguyen (SterlingBank - Head of ML), David Cooper (Platform), Marta Lopez (Security), Tom Briggs (Product)

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir with Redwood, i'm the AE, this is elena our solutions eng. we thought today we'd focus on workload characterization and traffic modeling for the POC. high level goal is to lock down success criteria, qps/concurrency targets, token distributions and timeline.
[00:12] Rachel: thanks, appreciate it. our goal is we want to run a two-week pilot to validate latency and cost before we commit to reserved capacity. key stakeholders are platform and security.
[00:25] Elena: great. quick q, is the pilot for text-generation-only or are you also testing embeddings/rerank?
[00:30] Tom: mostly text gen for chat summarization + a small reranking flow for fraud signals. embeddings are separate and lower volume.
[00:40] David: to be concrete, current prod has about 8 qps average and spikes to ~60 concurrent requests during business hours. networkwise we sit in us-east-1. we'd like to test with both bursty and steady loads.
[00:53] Elena: good, that's helpful. do you have typical input length / output length distributions?
[00:58] Rachel: averages are messy — median user message ~60 tokens, responses average 120 tokens but some long threads push to 600 tokens occasionally. 80% of traffic is < 200 output tokens.
[01:15] Samir: perfect. for modeling we usually capture: avg qps, peak concurrency, input/output token histograms, and percent of requests that require streaming or function calls. any function-calling in the flows?
[01:26] Tom: yes about 15% of requests trigger a tool call and we need streaming for partial responses in the chat UI.
[01:35] Marta: security note — data residency and audit logs matter. we need SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, and SOC2 artifacts. can you confirm Redwood supports these for private/dedicated?
[01:47] Samir: yes, we support SSO, KMS integrations, and we can provide SOC2 + pen test summary. if you do Dedicated or Private we can offer customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. i'll send the security one-pager.
[02:00] David: is there a difference in latency between hosted and dedicated? ballpark numbers?
[02:05] Elena: hosted will have slightly higher variability, p50s beneath ~120ms token gen for optimized models, p95 depends a lot on sequence length. Dedicated on pinned GPUs typically reduces tail latency by 15-30% for long-context workloads because of optimized batching and reserved slots.
[02:22] Rachel: ok our success criteria — we want p50 end-to-end <200ms for short ops (<256 tokens), p95 <600ms; accuracy parity vs current baseline (we use an in-house LLM) within acceptable drop (<3% delta on evaluation prompts); cost target around $0.0008 per output token on average. does that feel reasonable?
[02:45] Samir: that's reasonable as a target. we'll include two model variants in the POC: a quantized 13B (redwood-13b-q) and a 7B optimized (redwood-lite-v2-like) to trade cost/latency. we'll run throughput and tail-latency benchmarks.
[02:58] Tom: can you run a synthetic load that mirrors our 7-day anonymized trace? we can provide samples.
[03:03] Elena: yes — best is you share a 7-day sample of requests (anonymized) and we'll generate a traffic model: qps by hour, concurrency distributions, token histograms, and a synthetic replay that respects arrival patterns and session affinity.
[03:18] Rachel: timeline? we want to start pilot end of month if possible.
[03:22] Samir: proposed timeline: you share traffic slice by 2026-03-24; we spin up pilot infra + bench harness 2026-03-25 to 03-29; pilot runs 2026-03-30 to 04-13 (two weeks) with mid-pilot syncs. does that align?
[03:36] David: that's tight but doable. we'll confirm internal approvals.
[03:40] Marta: what exact metrics will you measure during the run? we need auditability.
[03:45] Elena: we'll capture per-request timestamps, p50/p95/p99 latencies (generation and end-to-end), throughput (tokens/sec), CPU/GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll provide logs and a summarized dashboard.
[04:00] Rachel: about token accounting — do you charge on input+output or only output?
[04:05] Samir: hosted default is input+output tokens. for the POC we'll provide clear token breakdowns and run scenarios showing sensitivity (e.g., if you reduce context window or enable prefix caching how it affects cost).
[04:18] Tom: you mentioned caching; how would prefix/KV caching affect our model choices?
[04:24] Elena: if you have many repeat prefixes or multi-turn conversations, KV/prefix caching can reduce compute significantly. for long-context threads we recommend a model with good KV cache behavior (we tested redwood-13b-q with 8k context and saw cost drop ~35% with caching enabled in similar workloads). note: numbers approximate and depend on hit rate.
[04:44] Samir: also planning: we'll test both streaming and non-streaming modes, and measure user-perceived latency via first-byte time and token waterfall.
[04:54] Rachel: are there any gotchas with quantized models and quality drop for our summarization use?
[04:59] Elena: sometimes quantization impacts rare-token generation or specific factuality. part of the POC is a small eval suite (you can share existing prompts) to measure quality delta. we typically run human eval on ~200 prompts plus automatic metrics.
[05:14] Tom: for concurrency modeling, we see spikes tied to batch jobs at 01:00 and midday peaks. we need the system to handle short bursts to 150 qps for 30-60s occasionally — can you model that?
[05:26] Elena: yes we'll build burst scenarios: 60s spike to 150 qps and a sustained 30-min high of ~40 qps. that'll exercise autoscaling and fallback routing.
[05:36] Marta: logging and retention — we can only share anonymized data. we need confirmation logs can be encrypted at rest and access audited.
[05:44] Samir: confirmable. audit logs and encrypted buckets are standard; we'll include requirements in the pilot SOW.
[05:52] Rachel: what's required from our infra to run the pilot?
[05:55] David: we need to know network requirements, firewall rules, proxies.
[05:59] Elena: we'll provide a connectivity checklist: outbound to Redwood endpoints (or VPC peering if dedicated), ports, sample curl, and if you want private deployment we'll coordinate pack install notes. we'll also provide k6 scripts to run locally if you prefer to push load from your side.
[06:15] Tom: bench specifics — besides latency/cost, we want to measure model throughput (tokens/sec) and batching efficiency. can you instrument batch size distribution?
[06:22] Elena: yes, we'll log batch sizes and effective tokens per GPU step. that helps explain tail behavior — if a lot of small requests prevents consolidation, cost / throughput suffers. part of our recommendations will be batching windows and API client-side knobs.
[06:36] Samir: for acceptance criteria let's capture as bullet points: one) p50 <200ms for <256 token responses, p95 <600ms; two) cost <= $0.0008/output token on average for production mix; three) quality delta <3% on your eval prompts; four) security checklist satisfied (SOC2, SSO, KMS).
[06:57] Rachel: fine. what about rollback or fallbacks if a model regresses?
[07:01] Elena: we'll set up canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a stable variant. for the pilot we'll show A/B results and a plan for automatic fallback routes.
[07:12] David: curious about telemetry — will you provide per-route dashboards and token-level cost breakdowns?
[07:17] Samir: yes, Redwood console provides per-route cost, per-model latency and token breakdowns. for the POC we'll grant a view into the pilot project.
[07:25] Tom: do you simulate cold cache scenarios? sometimes our traffic has long idle tails and cold KV misses cause big spikes in latency.
[07:33] Elena: yes we include cold start tests and measure cache warmup curves. we'll run steady-state and cold-start patterns.
[07:40] Marta: one security question — can we keep logs within our VPC or a customer-managed bucket?
[07:45] Samir: with Dedicated or Private yes; Hosted can stream to your encrypted bucket via customer-owned KMS. we'll document options.
[07:53] Rachel: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[07:57] Samir: recap: Samir — send pricing + SOW + SOC2 one-pager by 03-22; Elena — load generator & perf checklist by 03-21; Rachel/David — provide anonymized 7-day trace by 03-24 and confirm network peering details by 03-25. we'll schedule the engineering kickoff week of 03-30 and plan the pilot 03-30 to 04-13.
[08:15] Tom: sounds good. any blockers?
[08:18] David: internal procurement needs SOW and pricing; timing depends on legal review.
[08:22] Marta: security review might need an NDA for some artifacts but the SOC2 one-pager is fine.
[08:28] Samir: we'll send the standard NDA template along with the security one-pager.
[08:32] Elena: one more technical note — for accurate cost modeling please include sample ratios of short chat vs long summary vs rerank calls, and % of requests with function-calls. those affect batchability and token mix.
[08:46] Rachel: current split is ~70% short chat (<100 tokens), 20% medium (100-400), 10% long (>400); function calls ~15%, rerank 5%. we'll include in the trace.
[08:58] Samir: perfect, that gives us what we need to produce a realistic cost and latency model.
[09:03] Elena: ok we'll follow up with a modeling doc that shows modeled QPS/concurrency, expected per-model cost, and a recommended pilot config (model choice, batcher settings, caching).
[09:15] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll email the deck and SOW.
[09:20] Rachel: thanks, talk soon.

Summary (auto):
- Purpose: scope POC to validate latency, cost, and quality for SterlingBank's chat summarization and small rerank flow.
- Key metrics: target p50 <200ms (short ops), p95 <600ms, cost target ~$0.0008 per output token, quality delta <3% vs baseline.
- Workload: avg ~8 qps, short bursts to 150 qps for 60s, concurrency peaks ~60 with occasional spikes; input median ~60 tokens, output avg ~120 tokens, 15% function-calls, 5% rerank.
- Plan: customer to provide 7-day anonymized traffic slice; Redwood to produce traffic model, run two-week pilot 2026-03-30 to 2026-04-13 using two model variants and report dashboards.
